A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DP research work. Full text extraction and rendered-page comparison support comparison of the methods, equations, tables, figures, and technical appendices. V3 additionally contains a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V2 reports original DP evaluations on WebQSP, CWQ, and MetaQA, alongside ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark evaluations, ablations, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same SFT/KTO distillation, path generation and instantiation, constraint verification, and backtracking procedures. The appendix prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WebQSP, CWQ, and MetaQA datasets, with unchanged Freebase and movie-domain multi-hop question-answering coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in both the Table 2 benchmark comparison and Table 6 efficiency comparison. LightPROF remains the same comparator despite the revised numerical gap in the discussion.

E3.justification: Test sampling, H/H@1/F1 metrics, model configurations, two SFT epochs followed by one KTO epoch, and appendix settings remain unchanged. The abstract's Hit@1-to-H@1 edit is only an abbreviation change.

E4.justification: Component ablations, prior and error analyses, backtracking measurements, exemplar sensitivity, and successful/failure case studies are unchanged, including Sections 4.3–4.5 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly describes Table 6 as involving standard deviations as well as means from three runs; v2 stated only three-run averages there. Three-run/SD reporting already existed for performance results, and Table 6 still displays no SD values. This is limited additional statistical disclosure, not evidence of more runs.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated CWQ H@1 gap over LightPROF from 14.5% to 16.5%. This matches the unchanged Table 2 entries: 75.8 for DP with GPT-4.1 minus 59.3 for LightPROF equals 16.5 percentage points. No underlying table or figure results change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions in Section 2 and Equations 1–5 are unchanged. The added checklist marks theoretical proofs as not applicable without adding or revising mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about trustworthy reasoning, structural-prior distillation, constraint-guided introspection, benchmark performance, flexibility, and efficiency.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, result interpretations, and failure analyses are unchanged. The checklist repeats the existing manual-constraint limitation, automatic-constraint ablation finding, and proposed future automation.

D1.justification: The abstract's code address changes from the reml-group organization to mira-ai-lab. The checklist adds statements about README documentation for released code and models. These update access and documentation information; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: All 46 research references and Appendix A's related-work discussion retain the same cited works and positioning. Reference page breaks change, but research relationships do not.

P1.justification: V3 appends a 16-item NeurIPS checklist, adds a funding acknowledgment, and abbreviates Hit@1 as H@1 in the abstract. The main narrative and technical-appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The checklist adds formatted question-and-answer pages, while the expanded acknowledgment causes reference reflow across pages 10–12. All eight tables and ten figures retain their displays, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects a verifiable mismatch between Section 4.2 and Table 2, providing a small improvement in reporting accuracy, alongside updated access information. The checklist largely repeats existing material and does not supply the SD values it mentions for Table 6. The method and empirical support remain unchanged.
